newsitem.title: USA: One jobs report won't cause FOMC move - Fed's Meyer.
newsitem.headline: One jobs report won't cause FOMC move - Fed's Meyer.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer said on Sunday that one single report, even as strong as the U.S. August employment report, does not determine the outcome of a policy-setting meeting.
"A single report does not determine the outcome of a meeting," Meyer told reporters at the National Association of Business Economists conference.
Meyer was referring to the August employment report released Friday that showed 250,000 gain in payrolls and six cent hike in average hourly earnings.
Meyer said the Fed kept on hearing evidence about "tight labor markets and scattered wage increases" but the fact remains we have "rock-solid inflation" that has stayed at a steady, low rate.

Meyer said the Fed was focusing on the large payroll gain in August coupled with the low 5.1 percent unemployment rate that is taking us "outside of the range of the last two years," and a longer work week, and the higher earnings,
The next scheduled meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee, which sets monetary policy, is for Sept. 24.
